Holding the x pencil at 8 while producing 16 y rows per block may reduce threads per block from 512 to 128 and increase block-level parallelism, at the cost of loading four halo rows on each of four subtiles and thus duplicating halo traffic. Directly loading halo values with the established period-63 mapping also reduces the tile synchronization to one barrier. The competing occupancy, halo-traffic, and synchronization effects require measurement; no winner is presumed.
